Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract checkpoint: safeguard clauses for derivative use and feedback license

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As promised, attaching the current MSA + order form with our commercial redlines (high level) and our recommended language for IP/usage. Two asks now: (1) confirm which of your team will own final redlines and timeline for legal review, and (2) confirm whether Novum can accept the alternative feedback/training language we discussed (non-exclusive, limited feedback license + explicit opt-in for model training).

Key areas we flagged:
- Output ownership: We proposed customer keeps rights to their inputs and outputs for their productization, but we cannot agree to a broad assignment of outputs that would transfer IP to Redwood. Instead we offer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use generated outputs for service debug, safety, and aggregated quality improvements.
- Training/data use: Our standard is opt-in retrain. We can accept a scoped license to use aggregated, de-identified outputs for model improvements if Novum opts in per environment and dataset, and with a 30-day revocation notice.
- Feedback license: propose a narrow feedback license that allows Redwood to use anonymized feedback to improve models, not to claim ownership over customers' underlying content or product features.

Attaching: Novum_MSA_redlines_20271003.pdf (our annotated MSA), OrderForm-v2.docx (pricing + usage tiers).

Next steps I suggest: legal to legal redline exchange this week, commercial call if there are material changes to pricing or SLO that impact the order form.

If it helps, Laura can lead the legal call — Laura, are you available Tue afternoon PST?

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Appreciate the summary and the materials. Novum has reviewed at a high level and Legal has marked a few substantive concerns (see attached). Our primary asks: (1) stronger assignment/ownership language for generated outputs used to build product features derived from Novum data, (2) broader training permission so that Novum's anonymized outputs can be used to continually improve the model for features we pay for, and (3) a feedback license that permits productization of improvements created by collaborative feedback.

We are attaching our redline (Novum_MSA_response_20271003.pdf) that keeps a more expansive view of 'Outputs' and seeks an exclusive-like transfer for functionality built directly from customer data. That said, we're open to compromise language that gives Novum commercial certainty.

Timing: we need legal-to-legal resolution by Friday 2027-10-08 to hit procurement windows for Q4 rollout. If Redwood cannot accept assignment, please indicate precise alternative language and how Redwood will operationalize opt-in training flags and data segregation.

Regards,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Partnerships, Novum AI
On behalf of Novum Legal

Jordan / Markus —

Thanks Alyssa for the quick turnaround. I reviewed Novum's response and attached their redlines. High-level takeaways and suggested positions below.

Summary of Novum asks (quoted):
- "Assignment of outputs for product features created from Novum data"
- "Broad training permission across model pipeline"
- "Feedback license that allows productization of model improvements"

Our recommended positions:
1) Outputs: decline assignment. Instead propose a carveout that allows Novum to use customer outputs internally and to productize their own derivatives, but explicitly prevents a blanket assignment transferring ownership of the customer's original outputs to Redwood. We can grant Novum a license back for specific use-cases (e.g., to reproduce or benchmark) but not exclusive title.
2) Training: offer a scoped, auditable opt-in: a) customer can flag datasets/environments for training; b) logging and retention controls; c) a 30-day opt-out revocation plus deletion commitments for retrain artifacts derived from that data. This preserves Novum's desire for improvement while protecting customer content.
3) Feedback license: accept a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use anonymized feedback to improve Redwood models, with a clear carveout that excludes customers' underlying proprietary information and product-specific feature designs.

Suggested legal text snippets (for legal-to-legal exchange):
- "Customer retains all rights, title and interest in Customer Data and Outputs; Redwood is granted a non-exclusive, limited license to use de-identified, aggregated Outputs for the sole purpose of model safety, reliability, and quality improvement."
- "Training on Customer Data occurs only where Customer provides explicit, documented opt-in; Redwood will provide deletion and provenance records within 30 days of opt-out."

I can take point on the redline exchange — I propose we send our counter language to Novum as tracked edits and request a 30-minute legal call Tue 10/05 or Wed 10/06 to close the remaining points. Jordan, please confirm commercial tolerance for the opt-in and whether the procurement timeline Alyssa shared is firm. Markus — any fatal concerns from your side?

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Contract checkpoint: safeguard clauses for derivative use and feedback license

Jordan / Laura / Alyssa —

Thanks — I agree with Laura's approach. A few practical notes from ops/legal:
- We should avoid language that requires Redwood to "assign" Outputs. Assignments are one-way and create long-term operational burden for both parties. Propose instead: a narrow, revocable license for use-cases tied to the subscription and a separate commercial add-on for exclusive productization rights if the customer requires it.
- For training opt-ins, we will publish an internal runbook and add flags to our onboarding (account-level toggle + dataset-level consent). We can commit to providing provenance logs for any retraining activity on opt-in datasets.
- If Novum insists on broader rights, commercial should be prepared to offer a higher tier (Dedicated/Private deployment or an explicit buyout).

Alyssa — if Novum can accept the alternative path (revocable license + opt-in training + add-on for exclusivity), we can produce tracked edits by EOD Wed and schedule a Wednesday legal touchpoint.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
